title: Article 348 — Language to be used in the Supreme Court and in the High Courts and for Acts, Bills, etc.

content.overview: Article 348 provides that until Parliament by law otherwise provides, all proceedings in the Supreme Court and in every High Court shall be in English, and the authoritative texts of Bills, Acts, Ordinances, orders, rules, regulations and bye-laws at the Union and State levels shall be in English. A State may, with the President’s consent, authorise the use of Hindi or any other language used for official purposes of the State in High Court proceedings, but the judgment, decree or order of the High Court must still be in English unless Parliament by law otherwise provides. Where Hindi or another official language is used for State Bills/Acts, an English translation published under the Governor’s authority is deemed the authoritative text in English.
content.glance: SC and HC proceedings in English until Parliament otherwise provides. State may (with President’s consent) allow Hindi/official language in HC proceedings, but judgments remain in English unless Parliament provides otherwise.
content.study:
Article 348 language of courts and legislation:
(1) Until Parliament otherwise provides: SC and HC proceedings in English; authoritative texts of Bills/Acts/Ordinances/subordinate legislation in English.
(2) State may, with President’s consent, use Hindi or State official language in HC proceedings — but judgments/decrees/orders remain in English unless Parliament by law otherwise provides.
(3) Where Hindi or another language is used for State legislative texts, English translation under Governor’s authority is the authoritative English text.

Examination: English as default for SC/HC; limited State HC language option; judgments in English; authoritative English texts.

sections.heading: Key rules
sections.body:
1. SC and HC proceedings in English until Parliament otherwise provides.
2. Authoritative legislative texts in English (with translation rules for States).
3. State may, with President’s consent, use Hindi/official language in HC proceedings; judgments still in English unless Parliament provides otherwise.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What language is used in the Supreme Court and High Courts under Article 348?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 348, until Parliament by law otherwise provides, all proceedings in the Supreme Court and in every High Court shall be in the English language. A State may, with the consent of the President, authorise the use of Hindi or any other language used for official purposes of the State in proceedings in the High Court, but any judgment, decree or order of the High Court shall continue to be in English unless Parliament by law otherwise provides. Authoritative texts of Bills, Acts and related instruments are in English, with provision for authoritative English translations where a State uses Hindi or another official language.

examTips: English in SC/HC by default; State HC language with President’s consent; judgments in English.

keyTakeaways: Art 348: language of SC, HC, and legislative texts — English default.
